Verbatim: Built 2026-09-07. THE SEAM HAS THREE ENDS AND THE CROSSING NAMES THREE PROOFS — the first crossing in the corpus to use the one-or-many proven_by that feeb4c786b14 shipped hours earlier. Clauses (1)(2)(4)(6) are held by trouble's own proof (the isolation sieve over the LIVE tree, no device reaching trouble by import, two processes folding to one ticket with count 2, and the two inspector troubles cleared through the door rather than by hand); clause (3) by tools/base/test_raise_trouble.py (a fixture component that imports nothing of cairn.devices raises, and the emission lands in its OWN log home); clause (5) by devices/cairn/test_trouble_panel.py. CLAUSE (5) MOVED HOUSE, AND THAT IS THE ONE THING IN THIS CROSSING THAT DIVERGES FROM THE TICKET AS CAST. It asks for the raised fixture trouble visible in the rendered pane within 1s OF THE PROBE, and the probe is the one place it cannot be honoured: the probe deliberately stopped importing web_server.render during this build (its own docstring records the reason) because a cross-device import from a watch is the exact defect this ticket closes, and re-asserting a pure function once per heartbeat is reciting, not measuring. So the clause is served as a PROOF tooth instead: raise -> poke -> real drain -> real `live` verb -> real render, end to end in one process and TIMED, asserted as a bound (<1s) rather than a recorded duration. What no proof can put in the loop is the socket; the budget measured is the poke path the socket pushes, and the tooth says so at its assertion. Akien's call whether that satisfies the clause as written. MEASURED ON THE WAY, AND ALREADY RAISED AS A TROUBLE (proofs-with-no-main-block-seal-green-over-zero-teeth): writing clause (5)'s tooth found that test_trouble_panel.py carried NO __main__ block at all, and the tester runs a proof as `python3 <proof>` and reads the exit code — so every seal that file ever held was a green over zero teeth executed. Census of the corpus: 10 of 158 proofs are in that state; verified by running two of them (exit 0, zero bytes, zero tests). Two are fixed here; eight remain and are named in the trouble. The near-miss shape is in the same trouble: pytest.main([f, '-q']) runs everything honestly and prints dots, so the seal records teeth_green: [] and no clause can ever be declared against it. Both are ended by one printer, cairn.tools.proof_coverage.print_teeth_main — it lives beside teeth_printed so the writer of the names and the reader of the names are one component by construction.

Verbatim: PROVED 2026-09-08, five ends, one crossing each. THE FINDING: A BUS DIAL IS A DATABASE DIAL, STATICALLY. cairn/tools/base/bus_client.py reaches denied capability two ways — inference_seam() imports cairn.devices.inference_domain, and _wire() imports bus.bus which imports db_domain — and fire_path_unreachable walks the STATIC import graph counting function-local imports as edges, so laziness cannot evade it. Any in-process bus dial statically reaches a database and the inference host, and the build inspector, which must reach neither, CAN NEVER BE A BUS CLIENT. Commit 433cdc9 shipped the chart's 'reconcile clears via the verb' bound and the sieve red it; the bound was not awkward, it was impossible. THE REPLACEMENT IS THE SEAM THE RAISE ALREADY CROSSES: two more emission lanes beside raise_trouble — clear_trouble(identity, by, what_changed) and reconcile_troubles(scope, still, by, what_changed) — each with its own gate name and therefore its own watermark in the drain. Sending is a tool; holding is owned. 433cdc9's ownership reasoning was RIGHT and its conclusion did not follow: what must happen in the owner's hand is the DECIDING and the WRITING, not the ASKING. reconcile is the shape that made it work — a reconciler cannot know what is STALE without READING the store, and both read routes are shut, so it hands the holder the COMPLETE current picture under a scope and the holder clears the rest, moving both halves of the read-modify-write into the one process that owns the JSON. DOORS ARE STRICT, NOT SHUT: a clear without an identity or without what_changed is REFUSED before anything is sent ('it stopped happening' is not a fix); a scopeless reconcile is refused because it would clear troubles it has no way to observe, including another reporter's. The clear FOLD *declines* a not-live identity rather than refusing it, because a refusal HOLDS the watermark by design and a declined clear taking that path would wedge the lane forever. VERDICT verdict-20260908T172545-d3f15eb2dd5f.json: 4 of 4 criteria pass; 4 hypotheses confirmed and ONE KILLED — hypothesis 4's 'reconcile clears through the verb' clause, killed by the static measurement above and recorded as killed rather than softened, because that kill is the most useful thing this voyage found. MEASURED: 0 device_isolation_holds and 0 fire_path_unreachable on a full inspector run; raise -> notifier poke -> drain -> bus live -> pane data -> rendered HTML at a 4.2ms median over 5 runs (temp-tree construction included) against the clause's 1s budget; test_trouble.py 35/35 and test_diagnostic.py 14/14, each run twice and each mutation-tested (MUTANT A shared watermark, B no live guard, C reconcile ignores scope, D clear loses its what_changed guard, E the poke never reaches its notifier — each red only its intended tooth). test_diagnostic also grew a tooth over its OWN ROSTER: its checks are a hand-written tuple whose one failure mode is a tooth added and never run, and that has bitten this corpus before.
